info.title: higgsfield/higgsfield-kling-3-turbo
info.description: The request body Comfy Router accepts for the model "higgsfield/higgsfield-kling-3-turbo", and the response body it returns. The INPUT schema is the same schema the server validates a call against before it reaches the provider, so what is published and what is enforced cannot differ. The OUTPUT schema describes the provider's native result document exactly as Router returns it: Router does not validate, narrow or re-envelope the response, so the output schema is descriptive rather than enforced, and Comfy owns no output shape of its own.

schema.description:
Real wire request for Higgsfield's Kling 3.0 Turbo text-to-video endpoint. Turbo is a separate path variant rather than a tier of the v3.0 route, and its documented input schema genuinely differs from the std/pro/4k one: it REQUIRES `prompt`, adds `resolution`, and has no `sound`, `cfg_scale`, `elements` or multi-shot fields.
Comfy Router publishes and ENFORCES this schema for `POST /v2/models/higgsfield/higgsfield-kling-3-turbo`, which forwards the body below to Higgsfield untranslated. The alternate-provider leg `kling/kling-3.0-turbo?model_provider=higgsfield` is a different route with a different contract: it takes `kling/kling-3.0-turbo`'s own Kling-native body, is validated against that model's authored schema, and is translated onto this wire shape before dispatch. The two bodies are not interchangeable.

example.prompt: A cinematic glass pavilion in a misty pine forest at sunrise

duration.description: Output duration in seconds. Supported range: 3-15.

prompt.description: Natural-language instructions describing the desired output. Higgsfield documents that Kling uses up to the first 3,072 characters and truncates beyond that, so no maxLength is declared.

200.description: OK - the model's native JSON output, returned unchanged; the schema describes the provider's terminal result document as Router returns it.

schema.description:
Higgsfield's request envelope, returned BOTH by a generation POST (as `{status: "queued", request_id, status_url, cancel_url}`) and by the shared status route, which adds the output once the request completes. Only the video output is modelled here because the two enrolled families are video models; Higgsfield's own shared component also carries image and audio outputs for families Comfy does not enrol.
This is also the Comfy Router output schema for every Higgsfield video id Router publishes — `higgsfield/higgsfield-kling-3-{std,pro,4k}`, `higgsfield/higgsfield-kling-3-turbo` and `higgsfield/higgsfield-wan-3`. All five are SUBMIT-AND-POLL: Router polls the shared status route on the caller's behalf, so the body a caller receives is this TERMINAL document rather than the queued handle the generation POST answers with. A caller therefore reads `status: "completed"` with the download URL at `video.url`; `queued` and `in_progress` are in-flight states Router does not return, and `nsfw`, `failed` and `canceled` are the terminal failures. `url` is required on the video output, so a `completed` carrying no `video` is a contract break rather than a finished generation.

cancel_url.description: Absolute URL used to cancel a request before processing starts.

request_id.description: Stable identifier used for polling, cancellation and support.

status_url.description: Absolute URL to poll until the request reaches a terminal state.

url.description: Download URL of the generated media.
